result.summary: This PR bumps the Guix time-machine commit and updates several pinned packages (git-minimal, linux-headers, python-lief, python-minimal) to fix a Guix build failure on RISC-V caused by python-msgspec lacking riscv64 support. It also adds a manifest_gui.scm workaround that disables tests for python-psutil, python-pytest-xprocess, and python-sh, which fail when building python-lief natively on riscv64.
result.problem: Building Bitcoin Core via Guix on a RISC-V host currently fails outright because an indirect Python dependency of python-lief does not support riscv64-linux, blocking anyone trying to produce or verify reproducible builds on that platform.

open_concerns: A minor misspelling nit from maflcko ('builing' vs 'building') is cosmetic and not addressed as blocking.
maflcko suggested squashing the last two commits, a stylistic preference, not a substantive objection.
resolved_concerns: fanquake's initial aarch64 build failure due to an old rust package issue was resolved when hebasto updated the time-machine commit to include an upstream fix.
Guix builds by fanquake, willcl-ark, Sjors, and hebasto himself all produced matching SHA256SUMS across many platforms, confirming the update does not break other targets.

result.card: This PR bumps the Guix time-machine commit and several pinned Guix packages (python-lief, python-minimal, git-minimal, linux-headers) and adds a manifest workaround to skip failing tests in transitive dependencies, fixing a Guix build failure on RISC-V documented in issue #36232 ('package python-lief@0.17.5 does not support riscv64-linux'). The problem affects anyone trying to produce reproducible Guix builds on riscv64, a supported release platform. Four reviewers (fanquake, willcl-ark, Sjors, maflcko) independently reproduced matching SHA256SUMS across all target platforms confirming no regression elsewhere, and maflcko posted a review ACK on the final commit. The PR remains in draft only because the author wants to confirm his own native RISC-V build completes, not due to any reviewer concern. It overlaps with open PR #35855, which also updates the time-machine and may need reconciliation.
